risk:event_strength.title: Intrinsic unpredictability of strong El Niño events
risk:event_strength.our_title: The Pacific Ocean Pendulum: Why Strong El Niños Are Unpredictable
risk:event_strength.oneliner: The ocean behaves like a pendulum that sometimes swings to huge amplitudes and sometimes gets stuck in small oscillations, and the switch between these regimes cannot be predicted.
risk:event_strength.why: Shows strong El Niño events can be intrinsically unpredictable, so a measured very strong event is an important risk signal.

risk:fuel_charged.title: (Un)predictability of strong El Niño events
risk:fuel_charged.our_title: The Pendulum That Forgets How to Swing
risk:fuel_charged.oneliner: Strong El Niños can vanish for decades because the climate system flips between two distinct modes of oscillation.
risk:fuel_charged.why: Shows a model of equatorial Pacific heat buildup and release can make strong El Nino timing unpredictable, a caveat for this gauge.

risk:east_pacific.title: Forecasting the El Niño type well before the spring predictability barrier
risk:east_pacific.our_title: El Niño type can be predicted a year before the spring barrier
risk:east_pacific.oneliner: The difference in ocean surface temperature between the western and central Pacific in December indicates whether the next El Niño will be eastern or central.
risk:east_pacific.why: Shows El Niño has two types with different impacts and that the type can be forecast from a temperature difference across the Pacific.

risk:east_pacific.title: Impact of natural disasters on consumer behavior: case of the 2017 El Nino phenomenon in Peru
risk:east_pacific.our_title: A City's Pulse After a Natural Disaster
risk:east_pacific.oneliner: Bank transactions from six million Peruvians reveal how the 2017 El Niño shifted shopping habits and how quickly Lima's economy bounced back.
risk:east_pacific.why: Found heavy rain and floods during the 2017 El Niño changed consumer spending in Peru, showing economic disruption.

risk:peak_ahead.title: (Un)predictability of strong El Niño events
risk:peak_ahead.our_title: The Pendulum That Forgets How to Swing
risk:peak_ahead.oneliner: Strong El Niños can vanish for decades because the climate system flips between two distinct modes of oscillation.
risk:peak_ahead.why: Explains that strong El Niño strength and timing are inherently unpredictable, supporting the statement's caveat that past events are no guide here.

risk:world_ocean_record_streak.title: Recent global temperature surge amplified by record-low planetary albedo
risk:world_ocean_record_streak.our_title: Earth Took Off Its Sunglasses: Why 2023 Was Anomalously Hot
risk:world_ocean_record_streak.oneliner: In 2023, the planet absorbed more sunlight than in any year in the past 80 years, and it was this, not El Niño, that accounted for nearly all of the unexplained temperature jump.
risk:world_ocean_record_streak.why: Explains a recent global temperature surge by fewer low clouds, allowing more sunlight to heat the surface and ocean.

risk:warmer_next_year.title: Very early warning of a moderate-to-strong El Niño in 2023
risk:warmer_next_year.oneliner: Two independent methods predicted the 2023 El Niño with 89% probability and estimated its strength at 1.49±0.37°C.
risk:warmer_next_year.why: Shows El Niño warming peaks the following year, forecasting 2024 as hottest after the 2023 onset.

risk:warmer_next_year.title: Recent global temperature surge amplified by record-low planetary albedo
risk:warmer_next_year.our_title: Earth Took Off Its Sunglasses: Why 2023 Was Anomalously Hot
risk:warmer_next_year.oneliner: In 2023, the planet absorbed more sunlight than in any year in the past 80 years, and it was this, not El Niño, that accounted for nearly all of the unexplained temperature jump.
risk:warmer_next_year.why: Adds caveat that record-low cloud cover helped drive the 2023 temperature surge beyond El Niño alone.

risk:coupling_on.title: Modelling the coupling between ocean and atmosphere; the global signature of the El Niño/La Niña Southern Oscillation
risk:coupling_on.our_title: The Planet's Pulse with an Irregular Rhythm
risk:coupling_on.oneliner: Analysis of long-term El Niño index records reveals power laws and long memory that models miss.
risk:coupling_on.why: Explains that El Niño is a coupling between ocean and atmosphere, and that this coupling drives global impacts.

risk:coupling_on.title: Climate Networks around the Globe are Significantly Effected by El Nino
risk:coupling_on.our_title: Climate Networks: How El Niño Snaps Invisible Threads
risk:coupling_on.oneliner: El Niño barely changes average temperatures, but it destroys the connections between distant points on the planet.
risk:coupling_on.why: Shows that El Niño breaks links in a global climate network, so its effects can reach well beyond the Pacific.

risk:new_level_t2_world.title: Recent global temperature surge amplified by record-low planetary albedo
risk:new_level_t2_world.our_title: Earth Took Off Its Sunglasses: Why 2023 Was Anomalously Hot
risk:new_level_t2_world.oneliner: In 2023, the planet absorbed more sunlight than in any year in the past 80 years, and it was this, not El Niño, that accounted for nearly all of the unexplained temperature jump.
risk:new_level_t2_world.why: Finds the 2023 global temperature jump was amplified by record low reflectivity, suggesting a forced push into a new level.

risk:new_level_t2_world.title: Basin stability and limit cycles in a conceptual model for climate tipping cascades
risk:new_level_t2_world.our_title: The Climate House of Cards: Where Does the Stability Limit Lie?
risk:new_level_t2_world.oneliner: A stability analysis of five climate systems shows that above 4°C of warming, a state with four or five tipped elements dominates, and ice sheets play a key role in Earth's stability.
risk:new_level_t2_world.why: Shows climate subsystems can have multiple stable states and threshold tipping, so a persistent exceedance can signal a regime shift.

risk:models_below_reality.title: Using Network Theory and Machine Learning to predict El Niño
risk:models_below_reality.our_title: Network Warns of El Niño a Year in Advance
risk:models_below_reality.oneliner: The ocean whispers in pairs before it screams: a new hybrid forecast catches that whisper 12 months ahead.
risk:models_below_reality.why: Shows current El Nino predictions lose skill after six months, a caveat for winter forecasts.

risk:models_below_reality.title: Sensitivity of Indian summer monsoon rainfall forecast skill of CFSv2 model to initial conditions and the role of model biases
risk:models_below_reality.our_title: Why the February Monsoon Forecast Is Deceptively Accurate
risk:models_below_reality.oneliner: The CFSv2 model shows better skill for Indian monsoon forecasts starting in February, but the success is a fluke caused by a wrong La Niña prediction in 1983.
risk:models_below_reality.why: Gives a case where a seasonal model forecast La Nina while observations stayed normal, showing model bias can miss reality.

risk:warmest30_t2_world.title: Recent global temperature surge amplified by record-low planetary albedo
risk:warmest30_t2_world.our_title: Earth Took Off Its Sunglasses: Why 2023 Was Anomalously Hot
risk:warmest30_t2_world.oneliner: In 2023, the planet absorbed more sunlight than in any year in the past 80 years, and it was this, not El Niño, that accounted for nearly all of the unexplained temperature jump.
risk:warmest30_t2_world.why: Record-low planetary albedo from fewer low clouds explains part of the recent surge beyond known drivers.

risk:warmest30_sst_world.title: Recent global temperature surge amplified by record-low planetary albedo
risk:warmest30_sst_world.our_title: Earth Took Off Its Sunglasses: Why 2023 Was Anomalously Hot
risk:warmest30_sst_world.oneliner: In 2023, the planet absorbed more sunlight than in any year in the past 80 years, and it was this, not El Niño, that accounted for nearly all of the unexplained temperature jump.
risk:warmest30_sst_world.why: Shows record low cloud cover cut Earth's reflectivity, adding heat beyond trend and likely contributing to current ocean warmth.

risk:la_nina_after.title: Climate network suggests enhanced El Niño global impacts in localized areas
risk:la_nina_after.our_title: Climate Network: How El Niño Tightens Its Grip and Strikes with Precision
risk:la_nina_after.oneliner: A directed climate network shows that during El Niño and La Niña, the planet-wide impact becomes stronger but is concentrated in smaller areas.
risk:la_nina_after.why: Shows that El Niño and La Niña surface temperature impacts are localized and vary between events, cautioning against a simple global flip.

risk:global_next_year.title: Very early warning of a moderate-to-strong El Niño in 2023
risk:global_next_year.oneliner: Two independent methods predicted the 2023 El Niño with 89% probability and estimated its strength at 1.49±0.37°C.
risk:global_next_year.why: Forecast that the 2023 El Niño would raise global temperature about 0.2 °C, making 2024 hottest, matching the one-year lag in air records.

risk:global_next_year.title: Impact of natural disasters on consumer behavior: case of the 2017 El Nino phenomenon in Peru
risk:global_next_year.our_title: A City's Pulse After a Natural Disaster
risk:global_next_year.oneliner: Bank transactions from six million Peruvians reveal how the 2017 El Niño shifted shopping habits and how quickly Lima's economy bounced back.
risk:global_next_year.why: Peru bank data show El Niño changed spending and had a measurable recovery time, evidence of delayed regional economic impacts.

risk:global_next_year.title: Recent global temperature surge amplified by record-low planetary albedo
risk:global_next_year.our_title: Earth Took Off Its Sunglasses: Why 2023 Was Anomalously Hot
risk:global_next_year.oneliner: In 2023, the planet absorbed more sunlight than in any year in the past 80 years, and it was this, not El Niño, that accounted for nearly all of the unexplained temperature jump.
risk:global_next_year.why: Shows 2023 record heat was partly from low clouds, a caveat when attributing a year-after El Niño temperature jump.

risk:ohc_2000_record.title: The Rise and Fall of ENSO in a Warming World: Insights from a Lag-Linear Model
risk:ohc_2000_record.our_title: The El Niño Pendulum: How Warming First Amplifies, Then Damps It
risk:ohc_2000_record.oneliner: A simple delayed model explains why El Niño strengthens at first and then weakens under global warming, and lets you forecast its strength without running climate models.
risk:ohc_2000_record.why: Shows upper-ocean warming and stratification change ENSO strength, so a warmer ocean alters the system forecasts must read.

alert:price_soybean_oil.title: Solar Forcing of the Streamflow of a Continental Scale South American River
alert:price_soybean_oil.oneliner: For a century, the flow of South America's largest river has followed the rhythm of solar activity.
alert:price_soybean_oil.why: Finds Parana River streamflow in southeastern South America tracks El Nino, a regional measure of rain linked to soybean areas.

alert:price_wheat.title: Climate, Crops, and Postharvest Conflict
alert:price_wheat.oneliner: El Niño shifts political violence in African farming regions right after harvest.
alert:price_wheat.why: Research finds El Niño reduces early postharvest conflict in Southern Africa croplands, showing impacts are not only crop losses.

alert:the_share_of_models_below_reality_.title: Recent global temperature surge amplified by record-low planetary albedo
alert:the_share_of_models_below_reality_.our_title: Earth Took Off Its Sunglasses: Why 2023 Was Anomalously Hot
alert:the_share_of_models_below_reality_.oneliner: In 2023, the planet absorbed more sunlight than in any year in the past 80 years, and it was this, not El Niño, that accounted for nearly all of the unexplained temperature jump.
alert:the_share_of_models_below_reality_.why: Explains why recent warming was underestimated: a record-low planetary albedo from fewer low clouds added about 0.2°C that models missed.

region:west_africa.title: Impact of dynamical regionalization on precipitation biases and teleconnections over West Africa
region:west_africa.our_title: Monsoon under the Magnifying Glass: How Regional Models Change Rainfall Forecasts over West Africa
region:west_africa.oneliner: Regional climate models improve some monsoon-ocean connections and degrade others.
region:west_africa.why: Model biases in the West African monsoon and its ENSO teleconnection help explain the weak mixed rainfall signal.

alert:price_cocoa.title: Climate, Crops, and Postharvest Conflict
alert:price_cocoa.oneliner: El Niño shifts political violence in African farming regions right after harvest.
alert:price_cocoa.why: Finds El Niño and La Niña shifts change postharvest conflict in Sahel crop areas, supporting a climate to harvest link in West Africa.

alert:in_the_jun_issue_of_models_were_be.title: Climate network and complexity based ENSO forecast for 2026
alert:in_the_jun_issue_of_models_were_be.our_title: El Niño 2026: Two Barometers, One Forecast
alert:in_the_jun_issue_of_models_were_be.oneliner: Two independent methods gave conflicting forecasts for 2026, so the authors combined them into a probabilistic outlook.
alert:in_the_jun_issue_of_models_were_be.why: Independent 2026 forecast predicted neutral or weak El Niño, also below observed +1.80, so underprediction was widespread.

alert:in_the_jun_issue_of_models_were_be.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
alert:in_the_jun_issue_of_models_were_be.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
alert:in_the_jun_issue_of_models_were_be.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
alert:in_the_jun_issue_of_models_were_be.why: Explains how Niño 3.4 SST anomalies are estimated, so the observed ONI +1.80 depends on the anomaly method.

region:sahel.title: Oceanic Forcing on Interannual Variability of Sahel Heavy and Moderate Daily Rainfall
region:sahel.our_title: The Ocean Dictates the Rains of the Sahel
region:sahel.oneliner: Warm waters in the Atlantic and Mediterranean drive moderate downpours, while the Pacific Ocean, via La Niña, amplifies extreme storms.
region:sahel.why: Shows Sahel heavy summer rainfall is linked to ENSO, with El Niño tending to suppress moisture and instability.

region:sahel.title: Climate, Crops, and Postharvest Conflict
region:sahel.oneliner: El Niño shifts political violence in African farming regions right after harvest.
region:sahel.why: Measures ENSO effects on harvest-time conflict in Sahel croplands, noting early postharvest reductions.

region:north_africa_levant.title: Spatial Analysis of Seasonal Precipitation over Iran: Co-Variation with Climate Indices
region:north_africa_levant.our_title: Three Oceanic Conductors Control Iran's Rains
region:north_africa_levant.oneliner: Three climate indices explain where and how much Iran's seasonal rainfall deviates from the norm.
region:north_africa_levant.why: Measures Iran's seasonal precipitation response to ENSO, PDO and NAO. It finds the Southern Oscillation Index has the strongest effect mainly in winter.

region:europe.title: CNN-based forecasting of early winter NAO using sea surface temperature
region:europe.our_title: The Ocean Whispers Early: Neural Network Hears the Atlantic Winter Three Months Ahead
region:europe.oneliner: A convolutional neural network reads sea surface temperatures and predicts the European winter more accurately than linear models.
region:europe.why: Adds background on early winter El Nino to North Atlantic Oscillation links and notes models find them hard to capture.

region:north_america.title: Forecasting the El Niño type well before the spring predictability barrier
region:north_america.our_title: El Niño type can be predicted a year before the spring barrier
region:north_america.oneliner: The difference in ocean surface temperature between the western and central Pacific in December indicates whether the next El Niño will be eastern or central.
region:north_america.why: El Nino impacts differ for central versus eastern Pacific warming, so regional wet and dry patterns can shift.

region:russia_centralasia.title: Predictability of warm and cold winters: Assessment of El Niño effects in the North Eurasian regions
region:russia_centralasia.our_title: El Niño as Conductor: Why Winters in Transbaikalia Don't Follow the Pacific
region:russia_centralasia.oneliner: A warm or cold phase in the equatorial Pacific hints in advance what winter will be like in different regions of Russia: mild, harsh, or utterly unpredictable.
region:russia_centralasia.why: It measures El Niño effects on winter temperatures in northern Eurasia, informing how mild European Russia winters really get.

region:russia_centralasia.title: Predictability of climate anomalies in the regions of Northern Eurasia in the spring-summer months in 2024 in connection with El Nino
region:russia_centralasia.our_title: The Pacific Ocean Conducts the Heat Over Eurasia
region:russia_centralasia.oneliner: The transition from El Niño to La Niña in 2024 raised the probability of drought in European Russia to 67%.
region:russia_centralasia.why: It examines how predictable spring and summer climate anomalies in northern Eurasia are during El Niño, covering the spring signal.

region:southern_cone.title: Solar Forcing of the Streamflow of a Continental Scale South American River
region:southern_cone.oneliner: For a century, the flow of South America's largest river has followed the rhythm of solar activity.
region:southern_cone.why: It finds Paraná river streamflow rises with stronger solar activity and El Niño, backing flood risk in the Paraná basin.

region:andes_peru.title: Impact of natural disasters on consumer behavior: case of the 2017 El Nino phenomenon in Peru
region:andes_peru.our_title: A City's Pulse After a Natural Disaster
region:andes_peru.oneliner: Bank transactions from six million Peruvians reveal how the 2017 El Niño shifted shopping habits and how quickly Lima's economy bounced back.
region:andes_peru.why: Uses card transaction data to show how consumer spending and merchant activity changed in Peru after the 2017 El Niño floods.

region:andes_peru.title: Differential imprints of distinct ENSO flavors in global patterns of very low and high seasonal precipitation
region:andes_peru.our_title: Two Faces of El Niño: How Different Patterns of Ocean Heat Rewrite the Map of Droughts and Floods
region:andes_peru.oneliner: Eastern Pacific and Central Pacific types of El Niño and La Niña affect global precipitation differently, and this is only visible in the statistics of coincidences of rare events.
region:andes_peru.why: Finds eastern Pacific El Niño events coincide with anomalous rainfall over larger areas than central Pacific events.

region:pacific_islands.title: Differential imprints of distinct ENSO flavors in global patterns of very low and high seasonal precipitation
region:pacific_islands.our_title: Two Faces of El Niño: How Different Patterns of Ocean Heat Rewrite the Map of Droughts and Floods
region:pacific_islands.oneliner: Eastern Pacific and Central Pacific types of El Niño and La Niña affect global precipitation differently, and this is only visible in the statistics of coincidences of rare events.
region:pacific_islands.why: Measures how El Niño type changes where seasonal rainfall is very low or high, relevant to the Pacific dry and wet split.

term:lanina.title: Climate network suggests enhanced El Niño global impacts in localized areas
term:lanina.our_title: Climate Network: How El Niño Tightens Its Grip and Strikes with Precision
term:lanina.oneliner: A directed climate network shows that during El Niño and La Niña, the planet-wide impact becomes stronger but is concentrated in smaller areas.
term:lanina.why: It measures where El Niño and La Niña cause warming or cooling, showing these effects are concentrated in localized areas.

term:lanina.title: Modelling the coupling between ocean and atmosphere; the global signature of the El Niño/La Niña Southern Oscillation
term:lanina.our_title: The Planet's Pulse with an Irregular Rhythm
term:lanina.oneliner: Analysis of long-term El Niño index records reveals power laws and long memory that models miss.
term:lanina.why: It explains that El Niño and La Niña are phases of a coupled ocean atmosphere cycle with global weather impacts.

term:elnino.title: Intrinsic unpredictability of strong El Niño events
term:elnino.our_title: The Pacific Ocean Pendulum: Why Strong El Niños Are Unpredictable
term:elnino.oneliner: The ocean behaves like a pendulum that sometimes swings to huge amplitudes and sometimes gets stuck in small oscillations, and the switch between these regimes cannot be predicted.
term:elnino.why: Explains that strong El Niño timing is intrinsically unpredictable because the system shifts between oscillatory and chaotic states.

term:elnino.title: Climate Networks around the Globe are Significantly Effected by El Nino
term:elnino.our_title: Climate Networks: How El Niño Snaps Invisible Threads
term:elnino.oneliner: El Niño barely changes average temperatures, but it destroys the connections between distant points on the planet.
term:elnino.why: Uses climate networks to show El Niño breaks temperature correlation links globally, evidencing its wide weather reach.

term:elnino.title: Impact of natural disasters on consumer behavior: case of the 2017 El Nino phenomenon in Peru
term:elnino.our_title: A City's Pulse After a Natural Disaster
term:elnino.oneliner: Bank transactions from six million Peruvians reveal how the 2017 El Niño shifted shopping habits and how quickly Lima's economy bounced back.
term:elnino.why: Peruvian bank card data show El Niño rains altered buying patterns, grounding the local economic impact.

term:nino34.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:nino34.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:nino34.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:nino34.why: Shows how to estimate sea surface temperature anomalies in the Niño 3.4 region, the main measure the statement defines.

term:nino34.title: Forecasting the magnitude and onset of El Nino based on climate network
term:nino34.our_title: El Niño: Predicting Strength and Onset a Year in Advance
term:nino34.oneliner: A climate network in the Niño 3.4 region predicts the onset and strength of El Niño about a year ahead.
term:nino34.why: Uses temperature anomalies across the Niño 3.4 region to forecast El Niño onset and magnitude, supporting the region's central role.

term:nino34.title: Very early warning of a moderate-to-strong El Niño in 2023
term:nino34.oneliner: Two independent methods predicted the 2023 El Niño with 89% probability and estimated its strength at 1.49±0.37°C.
term:nino34.why: Forecasts a 2023 El Niño magnitude at 1.49 degrees Celsius, near the strong threshold of 1.5 degrees.

term:nino3.title: Forecasting the El Niño type well before the spring predictability barrier
term:nino3.our_title: El Niño type can be predicted a year before the spring barrier
term:nino3.oneliner: The difference in ocean surface temperature between the western and central Pacific in December indicates whether the next El Niño will be eastern or central.
term:nino3.why: Shows eastern Pacific El Nino events are a distinct type and can be forecast early, backing the dashboard's focus on the eastern band.

term:type.title: Differential imprints of distinct ENSO flavors in global patterns of very low and high seasonal precipitation
term:type.our_title: Two Faces of El Niño: How Different Patterns of Ocean Heat Rewrite the Map of Droughts and Floods
term:type.oneliner: Eastern Pacific and Central Pacific types of El Niño and La Niña affect global precipitation differently, and this is only visible in the statistics of coincidences of rare events.
term:type.why: Shows eastern Pacific events produce broader precipitation anomalies than central Pacific events, so their impacts differ.

term:type.title: Forecasting the El Niño type well before the spring predictability barrier
term:type.our_title: El Niño type can be predicted a year before the spring barrier
term:type.oneliner: The difference in ocean surface temperature between the western and central Pacific in December indicates whether the next El Niño will be eastern or central.
term:type.why: Shows eastern and central Pacific El Niño types can be separated early and that their regional rainfall impacts differ.

term:anomaly.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:anomaly.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:anomaly.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:anomaly.why: Explains climate normals as multi-decade averages and anomalies as departures from them, the same concept used for 1991-2020.

term:oni.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:oni.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:oni.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:oni.why: Explores how to estimate the climate baselines used to compute Niño 3.4 anomalies, which are the building blocks of the ONI.

term:nino4.title: Forecasting the El Niño type well before the spring predictability barrier
term:nino4.our_title: El Niño type can be predicted a year before the spring barrier
term:nino4.oneliner: The difference in ocean surface temperature between the western and central Pacific in December indicates whether the next El Niño will be eastern or central.
term:nino4.why: Uses an east-west sea surface temperature difference to indicate whether an El Niño will be Eastern or Central Pacific type.

term:analog.title: A Nonanticipative Analog Method for Long-Term Forecasting of Air Temperature Extremes
term:analog.our_title: How to Predict Heat a Year in Advance
term:analog.oneliner: A non-lookahead analog method predicts extreme temperatures with 100% sign accuracy.
term:analog.why: Shows an analogue method using past observations to forecast extremes without a climate model, though its focus is long term.

term:lead.title: Using Network Theory and Machine Learning to predict El Niño
term:lead.our_title: Network Warns of El Niño a Year in Advance
term:lead.oneliner: The ocean whispers in pairs before it screams: a new hybrid forecast catches that whisper 12 months ahead.
term:lead.why: Shows ENSO forecast skill normally falls beyond six months, the basis for treating lead 6 errors as expected.

term:lead.title: Entropic learning enables skilful forecasts of ENSO phase at up to two years lead time
term:lead.our_title: Council of Sages: How Entropy Predicts El Niño Two Years Ahead
term:lead.oneliner: An ensemble of entropy-based models, trained solely on satellite data, forecasts the El Niño phase up to 24 months ahead with skill comparable to the best dynamical systems.
term:lead.why: Measures ENSO phase skill out to 22-24 months, showing lead 6 is not a hard limit for all models.

term:soi.title: Long-term non-linear predictability of ENSO events over the 20th century
term:soi.our_title: A Map That Could Have Predicted El Niño
term:soi.oneliner: The Southern Oscillation Index holds enough information to forecast El Niño events two to four years ahead.
term:soi.why: Uses the 1878 to 2013 SOI record as an ENSO descriptor and shows it holds nonlinear predictability years ahead.

term:teleconnection.title: The link between North Atlantic tropical cyclones and ENSO in seasonal forecasts
term:teleconnection.our_title: The Overzealous Translator: Why Models Overestimate the El Niño–Hurricane Link
term:teleconnection.oneliner: Six European seasonal forecast models overestimate the strength of the El Niño–Atlantic hurricane connection, especially in the Caribbean basin.
term:teleconnection.why: Shows seasonal forecast models capture the ENSO to Atlantic hurricane link but overstate it, meaning it is statistical not deterministic.

term:teleconnection.title: Global teleconnectivity structures of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation and large volcanic eruptions – An evolving network perspective
term:teleconnection.our_title: The Global Climate Web: How El Niño and Volcanoes Rewire Temperature Connections
term:teleconnection.oneliner: A climate network shows El Niño shattering the global temperature hierarchy, while volcanoes act more locally.
term:teleconnection.why: Finds El Nino phases produce episodic breakdowns and strong teleconnections, supporting the usual not guaranteed framing.

term:teleconnection.title: Metastability, atmospheric midlatitude circulation regimes and large-scale teleconnection: a data-driven approach
term:teleconnection.our_title: Rooms of the Winter Sky: How the Atmosphere Chooses the Weather
term:teleconnection.oneliner: In winter, the Northern Hemisphere's atmosphere can spend weeks in one of four 'rooms'—stable circulation regimes—and the transitions between them follow hidden rules.
term:teleconnection.why: Links recurring mid latitude circulation patterns to teleconnections, showing the atmospheric rearrangement behind remote links.

term:trend.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:trend.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:trend.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:trend.why: Shows how climate trends bias simple normals and describes a filter to estimate anomalies after removing that trend.

term:trend.title: Limits on CO2 Climate Forcing from Recent Temperature Data of Earth
term:trend.our_title: The Tropics as a Clean Laboratory: What They Tell Us About CO2
term:trend.oneliner: Satellite data from 1979–2007 show that global warming stalled in 1998, and the tropical trend matches only the weak effect of CO2 without feedbacks.
term:trend.why: Separates a small underlying warming trend from year to year variability when explaining the 1998 temperature record.

term:t300.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:t300.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:t300.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:t300.why: Explains how climate normals and anomalies are estimated, and warns standard baselines can be biased in a changing climate.

term:weekly.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:weekly.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:weekly.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:weekly.why: Explains how climate normals and anomalies are estimated, using Niño 3.4 sea surface temperatures as a test case.

term:u850.title: Rotational and Irrotational Wind Forcing as dual drivers of El Nino Southern Oscillation variability
term:u850.our_title: Twin Winds: How Rotation and Divergence Drive El Niño
term:u850.oneliner: One part of the wind drives fast climate swings, the other drives slow decadal waves.
term:u850.why: Shows how equatorial wind stress shifts the ocean's warm layer, supporting the idea that trades are an engine of ENSO.

term:coupling.title: Modelling the coupling between ocean and atmosphere; the global signature of the El Niño/La Niña Southern Oscillation
term:coupling.our_title: The Planet's Pulse with an Irregular Rhythm
term:coupling.oneliner: Analysis of long-term El Niño index records reveals power laws and long memory that models miss.
term:coupling.why: Models the ocean atmosphere coupling that gives ENSO its global climate signature and distant impacts.

term:coupling.title: Redefining climate index with sea surface temperature of key area can better express atmospheric physical activity
term:coupling.our_title: An Ocean Thermometer Instead of a Barometer: A New Take on Climate Indices
term:coupling.oneliner: Redefining climate indices through sea surface temperature differences sharply strengthens their link to river runoff and points to a common astronomical driver.
term:coupling.why: Questions the standard SOI pressure index and suggests sea surface temperature differences capture atmospheric response better.

term:coupling.title: Coupled Ocean-Atmosphere Dynamics in a Machine Learning Earth System Model
term:coupling.our_title: Ocean and Atmosphere Learn to Speak the Same Language
term:coupling.oneliner: The neural network model Ola reproduces El Niño for the first time by modeling the ocean and atmosphere as a single system.
term:coupling.why: Shows a machine learning model reproduces coupled ocean atmosphere dynamics including El Nino, supporting the link.

term:pinksheet.title: Climate, Crops, and Postharvest Conflict
term:pinksheet.oneliner: El Niño shifts political violence in African farming regions right after harvest.
term:pinksheet.why: Shows El Nino shocks during the crop growing season change harvest related conflict only in exposed croplands, so impacts are local and seasonal.

term:pinksheet.title: Differential imprints of distinct ENSO flavors in global patterns of very low and high seasonal precipitation
term:pinksheet.our_title: Two Faces of El Niño: How Different Patterns of Ocean Heat Rewrite the Map of Droughts and Floods
term:pinksheet.oneliner: Eastern Pacific and Central Pacific types of El Niño and La Niña affect global precipitation differently, and this is only visible in the statistics of coincidences of rare events.
term:pinksheet.why: Maps how different El Nino types bring very low or high seasonal rainfall to particular regions, shaping agricultural production there.

term:pinksheet.title: Climate network suggests enhanced El Niño global impacts in localized areas
term:pinksheet.our_title: Climate Network: How El Niño Tightens Its Grip and Strikes with Precision
term:pinksheet.oneliner: A directed climate network shows that during El Niño and La Niña, the planet-wide impact becomes stronger but is concentrated in smaller areas.
term:pinksheet.why: Finds El Nino temperature links are concentrated in limited areas and much of the globe is unaffected, so impacts are localized.

term:dynstat.title: Knowledge-based Deep Learning for Modeling Chaotic Systems
term:dynstat.our_title: Taming Chaos with Physics: Predicting Extreme Events from Sparse Data
term:dynstat.oneliner: A hybrid neural network trained on synthetic data and physical laws predicts extreme events more accurately when data are scarce.
term:dynstat.why: Shows pure deep learning lacks data for extreme events, so it adds simulated data and physical laws to improve forecasts.

term:dynstat.title: Discovery of a Phenomenological Dynamical Model for Predicting the El Niño-Southern Oscillation
term:dynstat.our_title: A Trail in the Sand: How 135 Years of Weather Yielded the El Niño Equation
term:dynstat.oneliner: From a single long observational record, researchers extracted a simple nonlinear equation that predicts El Niño better than supercomputer models.
term:dynstat.why: Finds statistical and physics models miss nonlinearity, so a data driven nonlinear model predicts better.

term:dynstat.title: Hierarchical Testing of a Hybrid Machine Learning-Physics Global Atmosphere Model
term:dynstat.our_title: A Student Who Learned Physics from a Textbook
term:dynstat.oneliner: The hybrid atmospheric model NeuralGCM passes an exam on cyclones, El Niño, and anomalous warming, but stumbles in the stratosphere.
term:dynstat.why: Tests a hybrid machine learning model and finds it struggles with nonlinear responses under warming outside its training data.

term:tlt.title: Comment on "Influence of the Southern Oscillation on tropospheric temperature" by J. D. McLean, C. R. de Freitas, and R. M. Carter
term:tlt.our_title: El Niño as a Thermostat: The Accumulated Effect of the Southern Oscillation
term:tlt.oneliner: The cumulative Southern Oscillation Index explains half of tropospheric warming since 1960, challenging the dominant role of greenhouse gases.
term:tlt.why: Finds a cumulative Southern Oscillation index explains half of tropospheric temperature variation, supporting a delayed air response.

term:tlt.title: Modelling the coupling between ocean and atmosphere; the global signature of the El Niño/La Niña Southern Oscillation
term:tlt.our_title: The Planet's Pulse with an Irregular Rhythm
term:tlt.oneliner: Analysis of long-term El Niño index records reveals power laws and long memory that models miss.
term:tlt.why: Describes the ocean to air energy exchange during El Nino events, the mechanism behind the delayed warming.

term:pmel.title: (Un)predictability of strong El Niño events
term:pmel.our_title: The Pendulum That Forgets How to Swing
term:pmel.oneliner: Strong El Niños can vanish for decades because the climate system flips between two distinct modes of oscillation.
term:pmel.why: It uses a model where ocean heat builds and discharges, the idea behind warm water volume.

term:pmel.title: The Rise and Fall of ENSO in a Warming World: Insights from a Lag-Linear Model
term:pmel.our_title: The El Niño Pendulum: How Warming First Amplifies, Then Damps It
term:pmel.oneliner: A simple delayed model explains why El Niño strengthens at first and then weakens under global warming, and lets you forecast its strength without running climate models.
term:pmel.why: It shows that warming below the surface strengthens El Niño by increasing the layering of warm and cold water, so the ocean below the surface matters.

term:wwb.title: An improved noise model for representing westerly wind bursts in the recharge oscillator model of ENSO
term:wwb.our_title: The Noise That Rocks the Pacific Swing
term:wwb.oneliner: Bursts of westerly wind act like random pushes, and a new noise model explains why there are more of them before a big El Niño.
term:wwb.why: Models westerly wind bursts as wind stress noise that amplifies El Nino, with stronger events tied to more and stronger bursts.

term:eei.title: Recent global temperature surge amplified by record-low planetary albedo
term:eei.our_title: Earth Took Off Its Sunglasses: Why 2023 Was Anomalously Hot
term:eei.oneliner: In 2023, the planet absorbed more sunlight than in any year in the past 80 years, and it was this, not El Niño, that accounted for nearly all of the unexplained temperature jump.
term:eei.why: Finds record low planetary albedo from fewer low clouds boosted absorbed sunlight, helping explain the recent jump in Earth's energy imbalance.

term:iod.title: Coupling functions in climate
term:iod.our_title: Seasonal Climate Seesaw: How El Niño and the Indian Ocean Dipole Are Linked
term:iod.oneliner: A two-dimensional stochastic model with coupling functions shows that El Niño drives the seasonal variability of the Indian Ocean Dipole, not the other way around.
term:iod.why: Finds El Niño mainly controls the seasonal timing of the Indian Ocean Dipole, supporting the link.

term:iod.title: Indo-Pacific variability on seasonal to multidecadal timescales. Part II: Multiscale atmosphere-ocean linkages
term:iod.our_title: An Orchestra Without a Conductor: How the Ocean and Atmosphere Strike a Deal
term:iod.oneliner: A 1,300-year model run shows that slow temperature swings in the western Pacific control the strength of El Niño and monsoons.
term:iod.why: Shows El Niño wind patterns reach the Indian Ocean and set up the sea surface temperature pattern of the dipole.

term:iod.title: On the all-India rainfall index and sub-India rainfall heterogeneity
term:iod.our_title: Monsoon Season: How a Single Index Captures India's Mosaic
term:iod.oneliner: The all-India rainfall index reflects not the average intensity of downpours but the area they cover.
term:iod.why: Finds the dipole's effect on Indian rainfall is weak when El Niño is present, so the monsoon response is dominated by El Niño.

term:rain.title: Waxing and Waning of Observed Extreme Annual Tropical Rainfall
term:rain.our_title: Breathing of Tropical Rains: How El Niño Phases Drive Precipitation Extremes
term:rain.oneliner: Tropical rains swell and shrink in step with the phases of [tag:enso]El Niño[/tag], not just with global warming.
term:rain.why: Observed shifts in extreme tropical rainfall between wet and dry regions with ENSO phases support the drought and flood link.

term:rain.title: Impact of natural disasters on consumer behavior: case of the 2017 El Nino phenomenon in Peru
term:rain.our_title: A City's Pulse After a Natural Disaster
term:rain.oneliner: Bank transactions from six million Peruvians reveal how the 2017 El Niño shifted shopping habits and how quickly Lima's economy bounced back.
term:rain.why: Peru's 2017 El Niño floods changed household spending, showing how flood impacts reach people through the economy.

term:mjo.title: A Simple Intermediate Coupled MJO-ENSO Model: Multiscale Interactions and ENSO Complexity
term:mjo.our_title: A Bridge Between Typhoon and Current: How El Niño Is Born
term:mjo.oneliner: A simple model connects fast wind bursts, multi-year ocean rhythms, and decadal shifts, reproducing the full diversity of El Niño.
term:mjo.why: Provides a coupled model where MJO wind forcing interacts with ENSO, useful for the timing pushes.

term:mjo.title: A Stochastic Conceptual Model for the Coupled ENSO and MJO
term:mjo.our_title: A Bridge Between Ocean and Atmosphere Rhythms
term:mjo.oneliner: A simple model links the two major tropical oscillations and reproduces their statistics.
term:mjo.why: Models MJO eastward propagation coupled to ENSO, capturing wind interactions behind the timing pushes.

term:landbox.title: Climate network suggests enhanced El Niño global impacts in localized areas
term:landbox.our_title: Climate Network: How El Niño Tightens Its Grip and Strikes with Precision
term:landbox.oneliner: A directed climate network shows that during El Niño and La Niña, the planet-wide impact becomes stronger but is concentrated in smaller areas.
term:landbox.why: Near surface air temperature networks show El Niño warming or cooling is localized and varies by event, so fixed land boxes catch only some regions.

term:landbox.title: Forecasting the El Niño type well before the spring predictability barrier
term:landbox.our_title: El Niño type can be predicted a year before the spring barrier
term:landbox.oneliner: The difference in ocean surface temperature between the western and central Pacific in December indicates whether the next El Niño will be eastern or central.
term:landbox.why: El Niño type, eastern or central Pacific, can flip a region between dry and wet conditions, so box responses vary by event.

term:walkerraw.title: Tropical Atmospheric Circulations: Dynamic Stability and Transitions
term:walkerraw.our_title: An Air Pendulum Over the Pacific
term:walkerraw.oneliner: The tropical atmosphere behaves like a pendulum with two wells: it lingers in either a warm or a cold phase until an external nudge flips it to the other side.
term:walkerraw.why: Provides a mathematical theory of Walker circulation shifts between normal and El Nino states, supporting the collapse interpretation.

term:walkerraw.title: Intra-annual Principal Modes and Evolution Mechanism of the El Nino Southern Oscillation
term:walkerraw.our_title: Tug-of-War in the Tropics: How Seasonal Air Oscillations Drive El Niño
term:walkerraw.oneliner: Two dominant intra-annual modes of tropical air temperature are closely tied to the phases of El Niño and La Niña.
term:walkerraw.why: Finds strong coupling of the El Nino region to a second temperature mode in normal or La Nina phases, linked to a strong Walker circulation.

block:peak.title: (Un)predictability of strong El Niño events
block:peak.our_title: The Pendulum That Forgets How to Swing
block:peak.oneliner: Strong El Niños can vanish for decades because the climate system flips between two distinct modes of oscillation.
block:peak.why: Uses a recharge oscillator model to show strong El Nino events can switch unpredictably, so past events may not guide peak strength.

block:models.title: Discovery of a Phenomenological Dynamical Model for Predicting the El Niño-Southern Oscillation
block:models.our_title: A Trail in the Sand: How 135 Years of Weather Yielded the El Niño Equation
block:models.oneliner: From a single long observational record, researchers extracted a simple nonlinear equation that predicts El Niño better than supercomputer models.
block:models.why: Finds forecast models miss observed ENSO nonlinearity, causing skill limits; a nonlinear model improves predictions.

block:models.title: Intrinsic unpredictability of strong El Niño events
block:models.our_title: The Pacific Ocean Pendulum: Why Strong El Niños Are Unpredictable
block:models.oneliner: The ocean behaves like a pendulum that sometimes swings to huge amplitudes and sometimes gets stuck in small oscillations, and the switch between these regimes cannot be predicted.
block:models.why: Strong El Niño events can switch irregularly between oscillatory and chaotic states, limiting predictability even with good models.

block:models.title: A Hybrid Deep-Learning Model for El Niño Southern Oscillation in the Low-Data Regime
block:models.our_title: Navigator and Cabin Boy: How a Hybrid Model Learns to Predict El Niño from the Ocean's Short Memory
block:models.oneliner: A linear model steers the ship by the map, while a neural-network cabin boy learns from its mistakes, and together they predict El Niño more accurately than either alone.
block:models.why: Hybrid model corrects climate model biases and captures warm versus cold asymmetry, improving strong event forecasts.

block:radiance.title: ENSO and the Temperature of the North Equatorial Counter Current: An Ensemble Study
block:radiance.our_title: A Warm Current Against El Niño
block:radiance.oneliner: An ensemble of 52 climate runs shows that a 1°C warming of the North Equatorial Countercurrent triggers an atmospheric response resembling El Niño.
block:radiance.why: Shows how central Pacific sea surface temperatures drive deep convection and affect the Walker and Hadley circulations.

block:radiance.title: Tropical Atmospheric Circulations: Dynamic Stability and Transitions
block:radiance.our_title: An Air Pendulum Over the Pacific
block:radiance.oneliner: The tropical atmosphere behaves like a pendulum with two wells: it lingers in either a warm or a cold phase until an external nudge flips it to the other side.
block:radiance.why: Explains how the Walker circulation changes state and drives El Niño oscillations.

block:landbox.title: Climate network suggests enhanced El Niño global impacts in localized areas
block:landbox.our_title: Climate Network: How El Niño Tightens Its Grip and Strikes with Precision
block:landbox.oneliner: A directed climate network shows that during El Niño and La Niña, the planet-wide impact becomes stronger but is concentrated in smaller areas.
block:landbox.why: Uses near-surface air temperature networks to show El Niño warming and cooling is localized, not uniform globally.

block:type.title: Differential imprints of distinct ENSO flavors in global patterns of very low and high seasonal precipitation
block:type.our_title: Two Faces of El Niño: How Different Patterns of Ocean Heat Rewrite the Map of Droughts and Floods
block:type.oneliner: Eastern Pacific and Central Pacific types of El Niño and La Niña affect global precipitation differently, and this is only visible in the statistics of coincidences of rare events.
block:type.why: Compares precipitation extremes during EP and CP events and finds EP impacts cover larger areas, supporting a harsher eastern type.

block:type.title: Contributions of El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO) Diversity to Low-Frequency Changes in ENSO Variance
block:type.our_title: Five Faces of El Niño: How Fuzzy Clustering Explained the Shift in Variability
block:type.oneliner: Fuzzy clustering revealed five types of El Niño and La Niña, showing that the rise in variability after 1970 is linked to extreme and strong events.
block:type.why: Notes CP El Niño events are typically weaker than EP events, linking the eastern type to stronger anomalies.

block:type.title: Forecasting the El Niño type well before the spring predictability barrier
block:type.our_title: El Niño type can be predicted a year before the spring barrier
block:type.oneliner: The difference in ocean surface temperature between the western and central Pacific in December indicates whether the next El Niño will be eastern or central.
block:type.why: Shows EP and CP events have different regional impacts, with early type forecasts from Pacific SST differences.

note: vector finds what is about the same thing; the model decides whether it belongs next to the statement. A link means 'this is what the research says about this', not 'this is the source of that number'.
